lead: Cincinnati plumbing deals with old hillside housing, lead service lines and cold winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Cincinnati.
risk: lead and galvanized service lines, aging sewer laterals on steep lots and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, sewer laterals and frozen pipes
why: Cincinnati has a large share of homes built before 1940, especially in Over-the-Rhine, Clifton and Northside. Many have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron drains and long sewer laterals on steep hillside lots.
Winters freeze pipes, and heavy rain overloads the city's older combined sewers, which can back water into basements.
water: Greater Cincinnati Water Works draws mainly from the Ohio River, with groundwater from the Great Miami Aquifer. The water is moderately hard. The utility runs a program to replace lead service lines.
tips: Ask Greater Cincinnati Water Works about your service line.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Scope the sewer lateral before buying.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown, Over-the-Rhine, Clifton, Hyde Park, Northside, Westwood, Mount Washington and every other Cincinnati neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Cincinnati Department of Buildings and Inspections. Ohio licenses commercial plumbing contractors. The city sets the rules for home plumbing work.

faq.q: Is Cincinnati replacing lead water lines?
faq.a: Yes. Greater Cincinnati Water Works runs a program to replace lead service lines. You can look up your address online. A plumber can also check where the line enters your basement.
